answer: Picture a marketplace where every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Spinning up a thousand fake identities—one violet, one walnut, one umber—means posting a thousand bonds, and any that misbehave get slashed. The attacker now pays real capital per fake, not pennies, so forging a Sybil swarm costs more than the influence it buys. Honest agents reclaim their bond; cheaters forfeit it, making identity scarce and costly to counterfeit.
